mission_goal: Frank v0.1 voll lauffähig auf Andreas Ubuntu developer system

zero_cost_evidence.claim: NVIDIA Developer Program members have free access to hosted NIM API endpoints for prototyping; individual endpoints may be rate limited.
zero_cost_evidence.counterhypothesis: A configured credential can belong to a different billing or production context; request execution must still stay on the documented integrate.api.nvidia.com developer endpoint and emit a receipt.

request_bounds.claim: The exact serialized UTF-8 JSON request is capped at 2000000 bytes before runtime-environment snapshot, credential lookup or network access. This is a transport envelope, not a claim that bytes equal model tokens; model context limits remain provider- and profile-specific.
request_bounds.counterhypothesis: The provider can safely enforce its own context or body limit after authentication; falsified locally because a request above the runtime envelope reached the authenticated opener, while the repaired boundary rejects it before even reading the runtime environment and still accepts an exact-limit payload.

request_pre_serialization_bound.claim: Validated request text and message structure are checked against their exact default json.dumps size before the JSON document is materialized. The calculation includes the 66-byte fixed request envelope, 27-byte per-message structure, two-byte list separators and ensure_ascii escape width of every Unicode scalar. Requests above 2000000 bytes are rejected before serialization; the serialized UTF-8 byte check remains defense in depth.
request_pre_serialization_bound.internal_measurement: The repaired scalar-width function matched json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True) for all 1112064 Unicode scalar values.
request_pre_serialization_bound.counterhypothesis: Exact string escape widths plus a small structural lower bound are sufficient before serialization; falsified locally because 54793 minimal alternating messages fit the old character estimate but their separators and closed-schema object envelopes exceed 2000000 bytes and reached full snapshot plus json.dumps allocation.

request_pre_lock_scalar_bound.claim: For exact built-in request strings, the sum of model, role and content character counts is a conservative lower bound on default JSON size. A sum above 2000000 therefore fails before the global execution lock; the exact escape-aware serialized-size calculation remains authoritative inside the protected snapshot path.
request_pre_lock_scalar_bound.counterhypothesis: The exact pre-serialization check is sufficient even when it runs under the process-wide lock; falsified locally because a request whose built-in text alone occupied 2000008 characters acquired and held the lock for validation scans before its inevitable size rejection.

request_pre_snapshot_cardinality_bound.claim: An exact built-in message list is rejected before snapshot allocation and before the process-wide execution lock when its cardinality exceeds 54792. The bound is rechecked at the snapshot boundary because caller-owned mutable input can change after early admission. Under required role alternation, the densest valid 54792-message request with a leading system message occupies 1999978 bytes with the smallest valid model and explicit n=1; the next valid cardinality occupies 2000015 bytes and exceeds the 2000000-byte envelope.
request_pre_snapshot_cardinality_bound.counterhypothesis: Dividing the byte cap by the 32-byte smallest isolated message yields a safe maximum of 62500; falsified because that ignores required assistant-role width, list separators and the outer request envelope. A valid 54793-message conversation reached lock, snapshot and serialization before exact rejection.

output_token_budget.claim: Every v0.1 Chat Completions request explicitly caps combined generated reasoning and visible output at 4096 tokens. The number is a conservative local policy choice demonstrated in NVIDIA's reasoning example, not a claim that every task or model requires exactly 4096 tokens.
output_token_budget.counterhypothesis: Omitting max_tokens is safe because the provider default is an adequate bounded generation policy; falsified locally because the authenticated request contained no output budget, while NVIDIA documents max_tokens as the cap shared by reasoning and visible output and warns that budget exhaustion yields finish_reason length.

response_bounds.claim: A bounded read must request one sentinel byte beyond the accepted limit to distinguish an oversized response from a response that merely fills the limit.
response_bounds.counterhypothesis: Reading exactly the accepted limit is sufficient; falsified because HTTPResponse.read(amt) returns only up to amt bytes and therefore cannot prove end-of-body at that boundary.

payment_status_precedes_body.claim: A valid HTTP 402 status activates the current-budget-epoch payment hard stop immediately from response metadata; the adapter does not consume a non-200 body before status classification.
payment_status_precedes_body.counterhypothesis: Reading an error body before classifying its already received status is harmless; falsified because a stalled 402 body changed the outcome to incomplete_provider_response and suppressed the payment latch.

payment_hard_stop_atomicity.claim: For the single-instance v0.1 runtime, routing, authenticated execution and payment-latch publication form one process-serialized critical section; a waiting attempt re-evaluates the latch after the preceding receipt completes.
payment_hard_stop_atomicity.counterhypothesis: Independent preflight checks are sufficient for concurrent attempts; falsified locally because a second attempt reached the network while the first payment response was pending, before the shared hard-stop latch could be published.

bounded_payment_latch_state.claim: Payment-latch storage is limited to 1024 exact built-in string entries. Cardinality is checked immediately after the exact-set boundary and before element iteration, inventory membership, credential use or network access. At exactly 1024 entries, inventory fails closed as payment-latch capacity exhausted so a further provider response cannot append entry 1025; larger injected state is structurally rejected. The numeric limit is a local FRANK process-state budget, not a Python or protocol standard.
bounded_payment_latch_state.counterhypothesis: Exact built-in sets and strings sufficiently bound passive latch state; falsified locally because 1025 historical entries passed full element validation and reached authenticated routing without any cardinality policy. The repaired boundary routes with 1023 entries, fails closed without an opener at exactly 1024, and structurally rejects 1025 before element iteration.

payment_latch_evidence_separation.claim: Capability inventory reports payment_blocked_current_budget_epoch only when the exact provider and budget-epoch latch key exists. Storage-capacity exhaustion independently blocks eligibility as payment_latch_capacity_exhausted and cannot be represented as an observed HTTP 402 payment event.
payment_latch_evidence_separation.counterhypothesis: Every fail-closed route caused by payment-latch storage can be labeled as a current-epoch payment hard stop; falsified locally because 1024 unrelated historical keys produced payment_blocked_current_budget_epoch true and payment_required_hard_stop_active without the current provider/epoch key or any received HTTP 402.

payment_latch_inventory_snapshot.claim: Each capability inventory and its derived route evaluate payment-latch capacity and every provider membership against one bounded exact-set copy. A latch published after that snapshot belongs to the next inventory state and cannot partially alter the current claim.
payment_latch_inventory_snapshot.internal_measurement: A synchronized writer inserted the selected provider latch after capacity evaluation but before its membership test. Before repair, the same inventory mixed the earlier capacity state with the later blocked state; after repair, all rows represent the pre-write copy.
payment_latch_inventory_snapshot.counterhypothesis: Deriving route from one list of inventory rows is sufficient even when those rows read a live mutable latch set; falsified because a write during row construction changed membership evidence inside that single list.

payment_latch_validation_snapshot.claim: Capability inventory copies bounded exact-set payment-latch storage before iterating or validating its elements. Pre-copy and post-copy cardinality checks bound the snapshot, and later publications cannot resize the iterator or suppress the inventory receipt.
payment_latch_validation_snapshot.internal_measurement: A deterministic mutation after the first live-set element was consumed previously raised RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration and suppressed capability inventory. After repair, validation completes against the bounded copy while the publication remains visible only to later inventories.
payment_latch_validation_snapshot.counterhypothesis: Validating every element of the live exact set before copying is equivalent to validating the copy; falsified because a concurrent publication can resize the live iterator between those operations.

execution_latch_validation_snapshot.claim: Authenticated execution retains caller-owned exact-set storage only as the later latch publication target. Pre-route cardinality and element validation iterate a bounded copy, and route derives its state from a separate bounded snapshot, so a concurrent publication cannot resize the execution preflight iterator.
execution_latch_validation_snapshot.internal_measurement: A deterministic publication during the execution preflight previously raised RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration before opener access. After repair, the same mutation affects only the caller-owned source, validation completes on its copy, route snapshots the later state, and the valid request succeeds.
execution_latch_validation_snapshot.counterhypothesis: Inventory-only snapshot validation is sufficient because execute immediately calls route; falsified because execute performed a separate live-set element scan before route could establish its safe snapshot.

post_callback_latch_reauthorization.claim: Injected nonce and monotonic-clock functions are treated as executable caller code. After the final such pre-network callback returns bounded passive data, FRANK re-evaluates payment-latch state from the same environment snapshot before constructing or opening the request. A newly active hard stop, exhausted latch capacity or changed provider selection fails closed before network access.
post_callback_latch_reauthorization.internal_measurement: Deterministic nonce and monotonic-clock callbacks each inserted the selected provider's current budget-epoch latch after initial routing. Before repair, both authenticated opener paths ran and returned success. After repair, one bounded route snapshot following the last callback observes either mutation and raises payment_required_hard_stop_active with zero opener calls.
post_callback_latch_reauthorization.counterhypothesis: Reauthorization immediately after nonce generation closes every caller-code boundary before network; falsified because the injected monotonic clock still executed afterward and could activate the same latch while leaving that reauthorization stale.

post_network_payment_latch_publication.claim: A received HTTP 402 remains mandatory execution evidence even if caller-owned latch storage changes after authorization. Publication validates bounded snapshots before and after mutation, reports payment_latch_publication_failed when state cannot be safely committed, and receipt construction never performs live-container membership afterward.
post_network_payment_latch_publication.internal_measurement: On both ordinary-response and HTTPError paths, an opener inserted a hash-equal active string after preflight. Before repair its equality method raised during latch publication or final receipt membership and no receipt returned. After repair both paths return status 402 and payment_required_hard_stop, mark publication failure, and later routing rejects the corrupted storage before network.
post_network_payment_latch_publication.counterhypothesis: Pre-network exact-set and exact-string validation is sufficient for a caller-owned mutable latch throughout authenticated execution; falsified because the opener can mutate that shared set while the request is in flight.

failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.claim: If a received HTTP 402 cannot be safely committed to caller-owned latch storage, FRANK retains the exact provider and budget-epoch key in bounded process-local fallback state. Inventories using external storage merge validated snapshots of both stores, so repairing or clearing the external container cannot authorize a same-process replay.
failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.internal_measurement: After a deterministic post-authorization corruption made the primary latch write fail, clearing that external set previously allowed a second authenticated request in the same budget epoch. The repaired runtime reports publication failure plus an active fallback latch and rejects attempt two before opener access.
failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.uncertainty: The fallback is process-local and does not survive restart. Durable UnifiedDB-backed publication and an accepted Ubuntu live receipt remain required before claiming restart-level enforcement.
failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.counterhypothesis: Failing closed only while malformed caller storage remains present is equivalent to a current-epoch hard stop; falsified because the caller could clear the malformed element and immediately regain routing eligibility.

successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.claim: Every HTTP 402 latch safely published to caller-owned storage is also retained under the exact provider and budget-epoch key in the bounded process-local store. Inventories merge validated snapshots of both stores, so clearing an otherwise valid external set cannot authorize a same-process replay.
successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.internal_measurement: After a successful HTTP 402 publication to an exact caller-owned set, clearing that set previously allowed a second authenticated request in the same budget epoch. With process mirroring, the second attempt fails before opener access even though the external set is empty.
successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.uncertainty: The mirror is process-local and does not survive restart. Durable UnifiedDB-backed publication and an accepted Ubuntu live receipt remain required before claiming restart-level enforcement.
successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.counterhypothesis: A successful caller-owned latch write can be trusted for the lifetime of the execution process; falsified because the caller can clear the mutable set and immediately restore routing eligibility unless the observed HTTP 402 is independently mirrored.

payment_latch_durability_scope.claim: Capability schema 1.18 and execution schema 1.14 explicitly publish payment_latch_scope=process_local. payment_latch_active=true therefore proves only that the current interpreter process retained the provider and budget-epoch hard stop; it makes no restart-durability claim.
payment_latch_durability_scope.external_evidence: Python documents that threads share memory within one process. systemd separately provides StateDirectory for persistent service state and preserves those directories across service restarts. SQLite documents atomic transactions that survive application, operating-system or power interruption. Together these sources distinguish the current in-memory set from the persistent, transactional state mechanism still required for Ubuntu restart enforcement.
payment_latch_durability_scope.internal_measurement: A deterministic module-reload probe placed a synthetic current-epoch key in PROCESS_PAYMENT_LATCHES, observed it active in the first runtime instance, then loaded a fresh instance and observed the key absent. Before repair, a 402 receipt could report payment_latch_active=true without any durability boundary, while capability inventory and route likewise exposed latch state without scope. The new regression failed on all three missing or stale contract assertions before the fix.
payment_latch_durability_scope.counterhypothesis: An active process-global set is sufficiently durable for a service hard stop because systemd may restart the same service automatically; falsified because a restart starts a fresh interpreter state, while persistent service state requires a separate filesystem or database boundary.
payment_latch_durability_scope.uncertainty: This change prevents overclaiming but does not implement persistence. A restart-durable latch still needs an owner-approved UnifiedDB or transactional local-store schema, atomic publication before receipt success, cross-process concurrency semantics, recovery tests and an accepted Ubuntu live receipt. SQLite is research evidence for a possible mechanism, not a selected implementation.

post_cleanup_payment_latch_publication.claim: On the regular-response HTTP 402 path, latch publication occurs only after the foreign response context has completed its __exit__ cleanup. The receipt therefore cannot claim an active payment hard stop that response cleanup subsequently erased before returning control to FRANK.
post_cleanup_payment_latch_publication.internal_measurement: A deterministic response __exit__ cleared both caller-owned and process-local latch sets after the suite had published HTTP 402. Before repair, the first receipt still reported payment_latch_active=true while a second same-epoch request reached the opener. After repair, publication follows __exit__ and attempt two fails before network access.
post_cleanup_payment_latch_publication.counterhypothesis: Serializing the with suite through the execution lock makes latch publication inside that suite final; falsified because foreign __exit__ runs after the suite and can mutate shared latch storage before the with statement returns.

passive_payment_latch_container_boundary.claim: Every payment-latch storage path, including the process-global default and caller injection, must be an exact built-in set before capability inventory, routing or authenticated execution; set subclasses cannot execute overridden membership or mutation behavior around a received HTTP 402.
passive_payment_latch_container_boundary.counterhypothesis: The process-owned default can bypass the passive-container boundary because only caller-supplied state is untrusted; falsified locally because replacing that mutable module state with a set subclass executed overridden membership during ordinary routing and leaked its exception. Earlier executable evidence separately showed overridden add suppressing mandatory post-402 receipt publication.

passive_payment_latch_element_boundary.claim: Every caller-supplied payment-latch key must be an exact built-in string before capability inventory, routing or authenticated execution; a passive set container does not make polymorphic elements passive.
passive_payment_latch_element_boundary.counterhypothesis: An exact built-in set is sufficient to make membership and mutation passive; falsified locally because a contained str subclass executed overridden equality after both HTTP 402 transport paths and suppressed mandatory receipt publication.

execution_busy_timeout.claim: A caller waiting for the single-instance execution lock fails closed as execution_busy after 35 seconds and cannot reach credential use or network access.
execution_busy_timeout.counterhypothesis: An unbounded lock wait is acceptable because the active transport has its own timeout; falsified locally because a held execution lock blocked a waiting call indefinitely outside the transport timeout boundary.

passive_attempt_nonce_boundary.claim: An injected attempt nonce must be an exact built-in nonempty Unicode-scalar string of at most 128 characters before authenticated execution; string subclasses, lone UTF-16 surrogates and unbounded identity material are rejected before formatting or UTF-8 hashing so receipt identity cannot fail or allocate without bound after a provider request has already run.
passive_attempt_nonce_boundary.counterhypothesis: Any exact built-in nonempty Unicode-scalar str is safe bounded hash material; falsified locally because a 129-character injected nonce reached authenticated execution and post-response identity processing even though the production nonce is the documented 32 hexadecimal characters from token_hex(16).

receipt_clock_domains.claim: Execution receipt duration uses a monotonic clock that cannot move backwards, while an absolute Retry-After HTTP-date is compared with the wall-clock UTC instant at response receipt.
receipt_clock_domains.counterhypothesis: One wall clock is sufficient for both elapsed duration and absolute HTTP-date arithmetic; falsified because system-clock correction can make receipt duration move backwards or collapse to zero, while a monotonic clock has no UTC epoch for interpreting HTTP-date.

passive_monotonic_clock_boundary.claim: An injected monotonic clock must return an exact built-in finite float or integer before authenticated execution. Invalid start values fail before network access; invalid end values use zero duration and cannot suppress an execution receipt or run overloaded formatting and arithmetic methods.
passive_monotonic_clock_boundary.counterhypothesis: Any float-like value returned by an injected monotonic clock is passive duration metadata; falsified locally because a float subclass reached authenticated execution and then ran overridden __format__ during attempt-ID construction, preventing the mandatory receipt.

bounded_receipt_duration.claim: Receipt duration arithmetic is total and capped at 86400000 milliseconds. Nonpositive elapsed values become zero; a positive subtraction overflow, non-finite difference or larger elapsed value reaches the cap without suppressing or bloating the execution receipt.
bounded_receipt_duration.counterhypothesis: Validating each injected monotonic reading as a finite built-in number is sufficient; falsified locally because two finite floats produced an infinite difference and OverflowError after successful execution, while two exact integers produced unbounded receipt metadata.

bounded_attempt_identity_clock_boundary.claim: Attempt identity is derived from the stable request ID and a fresh 128-bit nonce, never from decimal formatting of an unbounded injected clock integer. Clock values remain duration telemetry and cannot suppress the mandatory post-execution receipt.
bounded_attempt_identity_clock_boundary.counterhypothesis: Including the monotonic start value in the attempt-ID preimage adds harmless uniqueness; falsified locally because an exact passive integer exceeded Python's decimal-conversion limit only after successful provider execution and prevented the receipt, while the mandatory nonce already supplies attempt uniqueness.

passive_wall_clock_boundary.claim: An injected wall clock used for absolute Retry-After arithmetic must return an exact built-in finite float or integer. Invalid and polymorphic values use the conservative 60-second fallback without executing arithmetic methods, reclassifying HTTP 429 or suppressing its receipt.
passive_wall_clock_boundary.counterhypothesis: Any float-like wall-clock result is passive timestamp metadata for HTTP-date subtraction; falsified locally because a float subclass executed overridden __rsub__, downgraded the regular 429 path and escaped the HTTPError path without a receipt.

text_message_roles.claim: The plain-text adapter accepts only system, user and assistant roles; tool/function messages require the separate typed tool-calling path.
text_message_roles.counterhypothesis: An arbitrary nonempty role can be delegated to provider-side validation; falsified for this adapter because it causes an avoidable authenticated network call before the provider can reject it.

exact_model_identifier.claim: The model field must match the model identifier served by NVIDIA NIM exactly and satisfy the shared semantic-text witness. Leading or trailing whitespace, embedded C0/C1 controls, and identifiers made only of format, mark, private-use or noncharacter scalars are rejected before credential use or network access rather than normalized or serialized into the authenticated request.
exact_model_identifier.external_evidence: NVIDIA instructs clients to use the id returned by /v1/models, documents nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b as a representative identifier, and permits NIM_SERVED_MODEL_NAME to override the served string. NVIDIA specifies no Unicode identifier grammar. Unicode classifies U+200B as Cf and private-use scalars as meaningful only by private agreement, which this closed text adapter does not negotiate.
exact_model_identifier.internal_measurement: An internally embedded JSON-escaped newline in mock\nforged passed the former local validation, reached the authenticated opener and could be echoed into a successful receipt. After the control fix, identifiers consisting only of U+200B or U+E000 still reached the opener. The shared semantic witness now rejects all three cases before network access, while meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct remains successful.
exact_model_identifier.counterhypothesis: Any nonblank Unicode-scalar model string can be delegated to provider-side validation; falsified locally because control-only and nonsemantic-only identifiers crossed the authenticated request boundary despite carrying no negotiated model identity.
exact_model_identifier.uncertainty: The semantic witness is local FRANK safety and canonicalization policy, not an NVIDIA identifier guarantee. Other printable Unicode identifiers remain permitted because NIM_SERVED_MODEL_NAME is configurable.

semantic_text_presence_boundary.claim: Plain-text request content, verified response content and exposed reasoning each require at least one Unicode-scalar character that is neither Unicode whitespace, a C0/C1 transport control, a Unicode General_Category=Cf format control, a Unicode Mark (Mn, Mc or Me), a General_Category=Co private-use character, a General_Category=Cn unassigned scalar nor one of Unicode's 66 permanently reserved noncharacters. These code points remain permitted around or within real text, but cannot alone satisfy the adapter's semantic-content requirement because this closed provider adapter negotiates no private character semantics.
semantic_text_presence_boundary.external_evidence: Python defines str.strip without an explicit character set as removal of str.isspace characters, so NUL, U+200B, U+0301, private-use characters, noncharacters and unassigned scalars survive; unicodedata.category exposes their Unicode general categories. Unicode Standard Annex #44 classifies Cf as Format, Mn as Nonspacing_Mark, M as the union of Mn, Mc and Me, private use as Co, and reserved unassigned code points as Cn. Unicode 17 conformance clause C3 says a process shall not interpret an unassigned code point as an abstract character. Unicode also defines exactly 66 noncharacters as permanently reserved internal values and private-use meaning as conditional on private agreement. RFC 8259 transport validity therefore does not prove semantic text. NVIDIA's current Chat Completions interface establishes no private-use or unassigned-code-point agreement with this adapter.
semantic_text_presence_boundary.internal_measurement: A user message containing only U+0000 passed the former strip predicate and reached the authenticated opener. Canonical status-200 responses whose visible content or parsed reasoning contained only escaped U+0000 each reached success, VERIFIED and DONE; the reasoning case also produced digest and character-count provenance. After closing C0/C1, U+200B and then U+0301 independently reproduced the same three failures. U+FDD0 then reached authenticated request execution and visible VERIFIED/DONE, while U+10FFFF reached verified reasoning provenance. U+E000 crossed request and visible-response boundaries and U+10FFFD crossed reasoning provenance. Finally U+0378, measured as Cn by the host Unicode 15.0 database and still unassigned in Unicode 17, crossed all three boundaries. The repaired shared predicate rejects all eighteen paths, while ordinary text containing these scalars around a separate semantic witness remains allowed.
semantic_text_presence_boundary.counterhypothesis: Preserving an unassigned scalar is sufficient to treat it as semantic provider text for forward compatibility; falsified for the current closed adapter because preservation and interpretation are distinct, Unicode forbids interpreting it as an abstract character, and U+0378 alone crossed all three verified boundaries.
semantic_text_presence_boundary.uncertainty: This is an explicit local FRANK text-adapter policy, not a claim that every control, format character, mark, private-use, noncharacter or unassigned scalar is invalid in all data. They remain preserved when another semantic witness is present. Cn classification is version-sensitive: the current host exposes Unicode 15.0 data, and a future Python/Unicode upgrade can assign a formerly Cn scalar; the regression pins U+0378 only while it remains Cn. A future typed adapter may authorize pure private-use content with an explicit versioned interpretation agreement. Tool, binary, multimodal and protocol-specific payloads require separate adapters. Modifier symbols remain deliberately unclassified.

unicode_database_receipt_provenance.claim: Every FREE_API_EXECUTION_RECEIPT schema 1.14 record names the exact Unicode Character Database version used by the runtime's semantic-text classifier. A host upgrade cannot silently present version-dependent Cn decisions as equivalent execution provenance.
unicode_database_receipt_provenance.external_evidence: Python exposes unicodedata.unidata_version as the version of the Unicode database used by its module. Unicode states that each published UCD version is stable, that new major versions can add characters or alter property data, and that precise character-property behavior should cite a full version. Unicode implementation guidance also notes that protocols can announce Unicode versions so newer systems can predict downlevel unassigned-character behavior.
unicode_database_receipt_provenance.internal_measurement: Execution receipts at the prior schema 1.1 head applied General_Category-based semantic admission, including the new Cn boundary, but contained no UCD version. On the current Ubuntu-compatible host the classifier uses Unicode 15.0.0; the same payload could therefore change admission after a Python/UCD upgrade while retaining indistinguishable receipt metadata. Schema 1.2 now records unicode_database_version on success and every classified failure receipt.
unicode_database_receipt_provenance.counterhypothesis: The runtime version or source commit is sufficient implicit Unicode provenance; rejected because neither appears in the execution receipt and Python distributions can embed different UCD versions independently of FRANK source bytes.
unicode_database_receipt_provenance.uncertainty: The version field identifies the classification database but does not authenticate the host, prove an untampered Python module or freeze future FRANK policy. Reproducible replay still requires the same runtime policy and UCD version.

receipt_schema_capability_advertisement.claim: FREE_API_CAPABILITY_RECEIPT schema 1.18 advertises the execution receipt schema version and active Unicode Character Database version before credential use, network access or model execution. Consumers can reject an unsupported provenance contract during capability inspection instead of discovering it only after execution.
receipt_schema_capability_advertisement.external_evidence: Python exposes the exact UCD version used by unicodedata. Unicode states that version changes can alter property-dependent program behavior and recommends a full three-field version when precise character-property behavior matters. Advertising the execution schema in the capability record is a local FRANK protocol rule derived from those versioned dependencies, not an external Unicode or NVIDIA requirement.
receipt_schema_capability_advertisement.internal_measurement: After execution receipts moved to schema 1.2, the capability receipt remained schema 1.1 and exposed neither the execution_receipt_schema_version nor unicode_database_version. A consumer inspecting only capabilities therefore could not determine the post-execution record contract. Shared schema constants now prevent literal drift, and capability schema 1.18 retains both values from the same runtime that constructs execution receipts.
receipt_schema_capability_advertisement.counterhypothesis: Capability and execution receipts are independently versioned, so consumers can infer the execution contract from source code; rejected because capability inspection is the runtime contract, the source or runtime version is absent from that receipt, and a remote consumer need not possess identical source bytes.
receipt_schema_capability_advertisement.uncertainty: The reciprocal version fields identify both record contracts but do not negotiate them, acknowledge consumer support, authenticate the host or prove that deployed code matches reviewed source. Older consumers must explicitly accept the additive capability-1.18 and execution-1.14 contracts.

execution_schema_capability_provenance.claim: Every FREE_API_EXECUTION_RECEIPT schema 1.14 record identifies capability_receipt_schema_version=1.18, binding the post-execution evidence to the capability contract that described routing, cost scope and quarantine semantics.
execution_schema_capability_provenance.external_evidence: JSON Schema publishes distinct dated specification versions and defines $schema as the dialect identifier against whose meta-schema a schema is valid. Reciprocal FRANK receipt-version binding is a local protocol rule derived from the same need to identify the contract used to interpret a record; JSON Schema does not require this particular application field.
execution_schema_capability_provenance.internal_measurement: Capability schema 1.18 already advertised execution_receipt_schema_version=1.13, but a successful execution receipt exposed no capability schema field; direct lookup raised KeyError. Execution schema 1.14 now emits capability_receipt_schema_version from the same shared constant that constructs capability receipts, while capability inspection advertises execution schema 1.14. The full 170-test suite passes after the failing assertion was retained as regression evidence.
execution_schema_capability_provenance.counterhypothesis: The execution schema version alone is sufficient to reconstruct the governing capability contract; falsified because capability and execution schemas evolve independently and the execution record previously carried no machine-readable capability version.
execution_schema_capability_provenance.uncertainty: Version binding is provenance metadata, not cryptographic authentication, schema negotiation, proof that capability inspection occurred, or proof that a consumer accepted either version.

cost_principal_capability_advertisement.claim: FREE_API_CAPABILITY_RECEIPT schema 1.18 advertises execution_cost_policy_principal_scope=process_local_credential_binding, execution_cost_policy_principal_restart_stable=false, fork isolation support and its child_pid_and_monotonic_parent_fork_generation context before any credential use or model execution. A consumer can therefore reject cross-restart cost-lineage assumptions during capability inspection.
cost_principal_capability_advertisement.external_evidence: Python documents token_bytes as cryptographically strong operating-system randomness and identifies 32 bytes as sufficient for typical token use. systemd provides StateDirectory as a distinct persistent service-state mechanism. Those sources support the measured distinction between the current ephemeral process key and a future durable service key; the capability field itself is a local FRANK contract.
cost_principal_capability_advertisement.internal_measurement: Execution schema 1.14 emits cost_policy_principal_scope=process_local_credential_binding and a module reload produces a different principal ID for the same credential. The prior capability receipt advertised only the execution schema and UCD version; reading execution_cost_policy_principal_scope raised KeyError, so pre-execution consumers could not discover the cost-lineage boundary. The repaired capability receipt exposes scope, false restart stability, the host's fork-isolation support and the exact fork context.
cost_principal_capability_advertisement.counterhypothesis: Advertising the execution schema version is sufficient because consumers can infer every nested field's lifetime from source code; rejected because the capability receipt is the pre-execution protocol boundary and neither source availability nor schema-specific inference proves process lifetime.
cost_principal_capability_advertisement.uncertainty: This is disclosure, not persistence, key attestation or negotiation. It does not authenticate the process, prove that the key remained secret, or provide a stable identifier across service restart.

fork_isolated_cost_principal.claim: On POSIX hosts supporting os.register_at_fork, every child process derives a domain-separated 256-bit cost-principal HMAC key from the inherited secret, child PID and a monotonically increasing parent fork generation before Python execution resumes. Parent and sequential children therefore cannot emit the same credential-bound cost principal solely because fork copied memory or the kernel reused a PID.
fork_isolated_cost_principal.external_evidence: Linux implements fork with copy-on-write copies of the parent's address space. Python provides before and after_in_child callbacks around fork. RFC 2104 specifies secret-keyed HMAC; FRANK uses a local domain, monotonically increasing parent fork generation and child PID as public context for one child-key derivation.
fork_isolated_cost_principal.internal_measurement: Before repair, a real Ubuntu os.fork probe produced identical parent and child cost_policy_principal_id 530d72f70db91014 for the same credential, proving that the supposedly process-local key was inherited. The final child callback derives a distinct key without a second entropy read; parent and child identifiers differ and capability plus execution receipts report fork isolation support.
fork_isolated_cost_principal.counterhypothesis: A module-global random key is automatically process-local because parent and child have different PIDs; falsified because fork retains the calling thread's address space and the untouched key bytes produced identical HMAC lineage in both processes.
fork_isolated_cost_principal.uncertainty: The guarantee applies only when Python's register_at_fork hook is available and control returns to the Python interpreter. It is not cross-restart durability, protection against an already compromised parent, or a substitute for a durable host key. Multi-threaded fork remains subject to Python and operating-system restrictions.

fork_entropy_independent_cost_principal.claim: Fork isolation does not depend on a fresh operating-system entropy read in the child callback. The inherited secret is transformed with HMAC-SHA-256 over a versioned FRANK domain, parent fork generation and child PID, so an unavailable token_bytes source cannot silently preserve the parent's cost lineage.
fork_entropy_independent_cost_principal.external_evidence: RFC 2104 defines HMAC as a secret-keyed construction. RFC 5869 documents HMAC-based derivation from existing keying material and context, while Python exposes HMAC-SHA-256 directly. The exact single-step domain design is local FRANK protocol policy rather than a claim of full HKDF conformance.
fork_entropy_independent_cost_principal.internal_measurement: With token_bytes forced to raise OSError in the child hook, the previous implementation printed an ignored callback exception and parent plus child both emitted aa439b4835ba83b3 while fork isolation remained advertised. The repaired hook does not call token_bytes after fork; the same injected failure leaves parent and child identifiers distinct, and all 166 tests pass.
fork_entropy_independent_cost_principal.counterhypothesis: A failed after_in_child callback aborts the child or clears the isolation claim automatically; falsified because Python reported the exception as ignored, the child continued, and the inherited key produced the parent's identifier.
fork_entropy_independent_cost_principal.uncertainty: The combined generation and PID context prevents parent-child and sequential same-parent PID-reuse equality but is not a global process identity, provider-account proof or restart-stable key. Fork from third-party C code can bypass Python callbacks.

fork_generation_prevents_pid_reuse_alias.claim: Sequential forks from one Python parent receive distinct cost-principal derivation context even when the operating system reuses the same PID. A before-fork callback advances a monotonic parent generation, and the child binds that generation together with its PID into the HMAC input.
fork_generation_prevents_pid_reuse_alias.external_evidence: Linux documents pid_max as the value at which process identifiers wrap around, so PID reuse is an expected kernel behavior. Python runs registered before callbacks before fork and after_in_child callbacks in the child. RFC 2104 supports secret-keyed authentication of the resulting domain-separated context.
fork_generation_prevents_pid_reuse_alias.internal_measurement: With getpid fixed at 4242 across two real sequential forks, the PID-only implementation emitted identical cost_policy_principal_id ecd020ebe0052459 in both children. After adding the copied monotonic parent fork generation, the same falsifier produces distinct identifiers and all 167 tests pass.
fork_generation_prevents_pid_reuse_alias.counterhypothesis: The child PID alone is sufficient context because live processes have unique identifiers; falsified because uniqueness among simultaneously live processes does not prevent later PID reuse, and controlled equal-PID forks reproduced identical lineage.
fork_generation_prevents_pid_reuse_alias.uncertainty: The generation is local to one interpreter lineage, resets on restart and is not a globally unique process identity. Forks that bypass Python callbacks remain outside this guarantee, and consuming a generation on a failed fork is harmless but leaves gaps.

fork_isolated_execution_lock.claim: On POSIX hosts supporting os.register_at_fork, a forked child replaces the inherited process execution lock with a fresh unlocked threading.Lock before Python resumes. A lock held by a vanished parent thread therefore cannot force every child execution into execution_busy.
fork_isolated_execution_lock.external_evidence: Python documents after_in_child as the callback point after fork and warns that mixing threads with fork can deadlock because only the calling thread survives. POSIX supplies fork handlers to restore application invariants in the child. Replacing this application-owned serialization lock is a local FRANK recovery rule derived from those boundaries.
fork_isolated_execution_lock.internal_measurement: With PROCESS_EXECUTION_LOCK held in the parent, a real os.fork probe found the copied child lock still unavailable after 100 milliseconds even though the owning parent thread did not exist in the child. After the shared child hook replaced that lock, the same child acquired and released it immediately. A later quarantine closes the distinct case where that held lock represented an unresolved authenticated request.
fork_isolated_execution_lock.counterhypothesis: Python automatically resets every application threading.Lock during fork; falsified because the untouched module-global lock remained locked in the child and the bounded acquisition returned false.
fork_isolated_execution_lock.uncertainty: This repairs only FRANK's application-owned execution lock. Python explicitly warns that multi-threaded fork remains unsafe; third-party C forks may skip Python hooks, and unrelated library locks can still be inherited. subprocess paths that immediately exec do not need or invoke this Python callback.

fork_during_active_execution_quarantine.claim: A child forked while FRANK's process execution lock is held is quarantined across every subsequently loaded runtime module instance in the same Python interpreter because the parent's authenticated request outcome and payment-hard-stop result are unknowable in the copied child. The child still replaces the orphaned lock, but execute_chat fails before environment, credential or network access; capability inventory and routing also mark every provider ineligible and select no route.
fork_during_active_execution_quarantine.external_evidence: Python warns that forking a multi-threaded process is problematic, exposes after_in_child for restoring child state, exposes Lock.locked() to determine whether the copied application lock was held, and documents exec as replacing the current process with a new program. Python's import system permits distinct module objects, and register_at_fork runs child callbacks in registration order without offering unregistration. Python's data model and accepted PEP 562 specify paired module-level __getattr__ and __dir__ hooks: __dir__ must represent names accessible on the module. Sharing and dynamically reading the quarantine through one already-loaded interpreter module is a local FRANK safety mechanism derived from those boundaries, not a Python security primitive.
fork_during_active_execution_quarantine.internal_measurement: A background thread was held inside one runtime instance's authenticated opener while the main thread performed a real fork. A second runtime instance loaded before that request kept its earlier module-local false snapshot even after the active instance's child callback set the shared latch: it selected NVIDIA and reached its injected opener, yielding unreachable_provider:True. After execution paths switched to live shared-state reads, that preloaded module's legacy exported PROCESS_FORK_ACTIVE_EXECUTION_QUARANTINED attribute still contradicted its own receipt as false. Dynamic __getattr__ fixed its value but the standard dir(module) introspection then omitted the accessible compatibility name. The runtime now resolves execution decisions and that compatibility attribute dynamically from the shared latch, exposes the name through module __dir__, and provides the public live function is_fork_active_execution_quarantined so imported consumers need not retain a copied Boolean. Capability schema 1.18 announces that accessor while execution schema 1.14 continues to publish fork_active_execution_quarantine_scope=python_interpreter_shared_state; all 170 tests pass.
fork_during_active_execution_quarantine.counterhypothesis: Dynamic __getattr__ alone fully preserves the exported compatibility surface; falsified twice: the former module-global returned a stale false value, and after its removal dir(module) omitted the still-accessible name until paired __dir__ support was added.
fork_during_active_execution_quarantine.uncertainty: Python itself deprecates multi-threaded os.fork use and warns of deadlocks. The quarantine is shared within one interpreter but is not authenticated against hostile same-process mutation, does not claim coverage across subinterpreters, and does not repair unrelated library locks, coordinate with the parent, produce cross-process exactly-once semantics or cover forks that bypass Python callbacks. Recovery requires exec or process restart.

model_availability_capability_scope.claim: A provider-level free endpoint capability does not establish that an arbitrary requested model is currently available. Every unprobed inventory row therefore records model_availability_verified=false, and the capability receipt explicitly denies inferring model availability without a probe.
model_availability_capability_scope.external_evidence: NVIDIA describes its catalog as free serverless APIs for development, but its current model pages expose availability per model. The official gpt-oss-20b page reports Free Endpoint Available, while current GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro pages report Free Endpoint Deprecated. Provider endpoint cost evidence therefore cannot prove deployment of every model identifier.
model_availability_capability_scope.internal_measurement: The prior capability schema marked NVIDIA zero_cost_assured=true and eligible=true from provider-level evidence but contained no separate model-availability state. Because inventory and receipt accept no model identifier and perform no network probe, a consumer could not distinguish endpoint eligibility from concrete model availability. Schema 1.3 now makes that missing evidence explicit without claiming a failed model probe.
model_availability_capability_scope.counterhypothesis: A configured free NVIDIA endpoint implies every syntactically valid requested model is available; falsified by NVIDIA's simultaneous model-specific Available and Deprecated states.
model_availability_capability_scope.uncertainty: This change improves claim scope but does not discover a usable model. A future cost-zero model discovery protocol must bind a fresh model-list or catalog observation to its endpoint, time and model identifier without promoting partner or paid availability. No NVIDIA credential is present on this host, so no live probe or model execution was attempted.

provider_route_scope.claim: A configured route selects only an eligible provider endpoint, not a concrete available model. FREE_API_CAPABILITY_RECEIPT schema 1.18 therefore marks every route with selection_scope=provider_endpoint and model_availability_verified=false until separate model-bound executable evidence exists.
provider_route_scope.external_evidence: NVIDIA documents GET /v1/models as a separate operation that lists models currently loaded and available for inference, while its model catalog presents model-specific endpoints and availability. Selecting the NVIDIA provider endpoint is therefore not equivalent to observing any particular model in that endpoint's current model set.
provider_route_scope.internal_measurement: With a syntactically valid NVIDIA credential, the prior route returned selected=nvidia while every unprobed inventory row correctly retained model_availability_verified=false. Because the route omitted its selection scope and availability state, a consumer could overread selected as model-ready. The regression first raised KeyError for selection_scope; the fixed route explicitly reports provider_endpoint scope and false model availability.
provider_route_scope.counterhypothesis: Choosing an eligible provider route also proves the requested model is available; falsified because NVIDIA exposes current model availability through a distinct /v1/models observation and the capability route performs no model-bound network probe.
provider_route_scope.uncertainty: This field closes an inference gap but performs no discovery. A future zero-cost model probe must bind provider origin, exact model identifier, observation time and cost status; a later successful execution remains request-bounded rather than a durable availability guarantee.

model_availability_execution_evidence.claim: FREE_API_EXECUTION_RECEIPT schema 1.14 sets model_availability_verified=true only when the requested model produced a fully typed success response that crossed VERIFIED and DONE. Provider errors, rate limits, pending responses, malformed bodies and transport failures retain false because none proves successful availability of that model.
model_availability_execution_evidence.external_evidence: NVIDIA's current gpt-oss-20b page identifies the exact model string, the integrate.api.nvidia.com Chat Completions endpoint and Free Endpoint Available as separate facts. A validated completion for that requested identifier is executable availability evidence at the observation time; provider-level catalog or endpoint evidence alone is not.
model_availability_execution_evidence.internal_measurement: The prior execution schema recorded the requested model and final outcome but lacked an explicit availability-evidence field, while capability schema 1.3 already stated that unprobed availability was false. The regression contrasts an exact valid status-200 completion with HTTP 500: only the former now sets model_availability_verified=true.
model_availability_execution_evidence.counterhypothesis: Any received provider response proves model availability; falsified because HTTP 500 can be produced by routing, infrastructure or provider failures without a valid completion from the requested model.
model_availability_execution_evidence.uncertainty: A successful response proves only observed availability for this bounded request and time. It does not guarantee future uptime, remaining quota, model immutability, provider authorship or zero monetary cost independently of the separately bound endpoint-cost policy.

canonical_blob_write_boundary.claim: A successful repository contents write is not accepted as canonical evidence until the returned remote content blob SHA exactly matches git hash-object for the intended local bytes. Large replacement files are assembled from bounded lossless chunks before the write; textual success alone cannot establish byte identity.
canonical_blob_write_boundary.external_evidence: GitHub's Contents API returns the resulting content object's sha separately from the commit SHA. Git documents git hash-object as computing the blob object ID from a file's contents and defines a blob object ID over its type, byte size and bytes.
canonical_blob_write_boundary.internal_measurement: A whole-file connector write reported success but its returned blob SHA 932f845e did not match the intended local blob e2b8e662. Remote line-range inspection showed the committed test file ended at line 4098 while the intended suite had 5104 lines: the intermediate command output had been truncated before the write. A first chunk repair was deliberately rejected because redundant join newlines produced cc94fcca. Concatenating bounded chunks without modification produced the exact expected remote blob e2b8e662. A later hard-coded 5201-line transfer of a 5202-line combining-mark falsifier similarly produced 9d170896 and was rejected; the complete rerun produced the intended b0ca233e. In the same cycle a stale 1499-line runtime bound omitted line 1500 and produced 606ef0ad instead of 236fb6d1, while a capped policy transfer stopped at line 1108 of 1130 and produced 36e79792 instead of 97ef255a; both writes were rejected and repaired from complete bounded chunks.
canonical_blob_write_boundary.counterhypothesis: A successful Contents API response proves that the caller's intended complete bytes were committed; falsified because the API correctly committed the truncated bytes it received and returned success, while only the content-SHA comparison exposed the upstream truncation.
canonical_blob_write_boundary.uncertainty: This operational invariant detects byte divergence but does not by itself prove semantic correctness, review quality or CI execution. SHA-1 collision resistance is not treated as an authorship guarantee; within this workflow the equality check is an integrity discriminator between two directly measured byte sequences.

bearer_credential_syntax.claim: A configured provider credential is routable only when it is at most 8192 characters and matches the RFC 6750 b64token grammar before normalization, scanning or Authorization-header construction; oversized values, whitespace, CR/LF, non-ASCII and other separators fail closed before network access.
bearer_credential_syntax.counterhypothesis: A syntactically valid b64token is automatically bounded credential evidence and the HTTP stack can impose limits later; falsified because an 8193-character value was selected for authenticated routing and reached header construction, while the exact 8192-character policy boundary remains accepted.

credential_cost_principal_binding.claim: Execution schema 1.14 binds cost_policy_principal_id to the exact validated credential through a domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 pseudonym keyed by a fresh 256-bit process secret; forked children derive a domain-separated child key from that secret without requiring a second entropy read. Rotating a credential changes cost lineage without serializing it, while a receipt alone no longer supplies a deterministic offline verifier for guessed credential values. Receipts explicitly scope the handle as process_local_credential_binding rather than a verified provider account identity.
credential_cost_principal_binding.external_evidence: RFC 2104 and Python define HMAC with distinct key and message inputs; Python secrets supplies operating-system cryptographic randomness suitable for secret management. NIST requires password verifiers to resist offline guessing; that requirement is analogous threat guidance rather than a direct API-token storage rule. The repo-native cost-principal research required a host-held opaque handle or keyed pseudonym and explicitly rejected treating provider/key-name identity as billing-account identity.
credential_cost_principal_binding.internal_measurement: The first repair correctly separated two rotated credentials, but used the credential as HMAC key over a completely public message. A receipt-only test recomputed the exact published cost_policy_principal_id fad403426b45679e from one guessed credential and public context. With a random non-receipted process key, the same public calculation no longer matches; credential rotation still changes lineage, and loading a fresh runtime produces a distinct principal ID for the same credential.
credential_cost_principal_binding.counterhypothesis: Using the bearer credential itself as the HMAC key hides it because HMAC is keyed; falsified because the authenticated message and downstream hash input were public, so each guessed credential deterministically reproduced or rejected the receipt value offline.
credential_cost_principal_binding.uncertainty: The repaired HMAC handle distinguishes credential bytes only within one process. It intentionally changes after restart and still does not prove provider account, billing principal, project, entitlement, owner or current zero-cost balance. A restart-stable opaque handle requires separate durable host key management and owner-approved state semantics.

dual_request_cost_identity.claim: Execution schema 1.14 separates a credential-independent semantic_request_id from the process-local credential-bound request_id and cost_policy_principal_id. Equal serialized requests to the same provider endpoint retain semantic correlation across credential rotation, while different payloads and different cost authorities retain distinct execution lineage.
dual_request_cost_identity.external_evidence: RFC 9110 permits automatic retry of a non-idempotent method only with independent knowledge that its semantics are idempotent or that the original request was never applied. The current expired IETF Idempotency-Key draft defines a separate client value that a resource processes to recognize retries; FRANK sends no such provider-supported header. The repo-native cost-boundary research requires separate semantic and cost/execution identities.
dual_request_cost_identity.internal_measurement: Before repair, rotating the credential for an otherwise identical validated request changed the only request_id, and no field preserved semantic correlation. After repair, the two receipts retain one semantic_request_id while cost_policy_principal_id and request_id differ. Two equal-length requests whose content differs retain different semantic_request_id values.
dual_request_cost_identity.counterhypothesis: One cost-bound request identifier is sufficient for both semantic correlation and payment authority; falsified because credential rotation either destroys semantic continuity or, if omitted from identity, aliases potentially different billing authorities.
dual_request_cost_identity.uncertainty: semantic_request_id is a local digest-derived correlation handle, not provider acknowledgement, authorship, exactly-once execution, replay authorization or an Idempotency-Key. A retry remains forbidden unless separate provider-supported idempotency or proof of non-application exists.

incomplete_body_errors.claim: http.client.IncompleteRead after a received response is an incomplete provider response, not an unhandled process exception.
incomplete_body_errors.counterhypothesis: Timeout handling covers every interrupted body read; falsified because IncompleteRead is an HTTPException rather than TimeoutError or URLError and escaped without a receipt.

pre_response_disconnects.claim: A ConnectionError such as http.client.RemoteDisconnected before response headers is an unreachable provider attempt with null status and no EXECUTED state.
pre_response_disconnects.counterhypothesis: urllib always wraps remote disconnects in URLError; falsified by the executable opener path where RemoteDisconnected escaped directly without a receipt.

malformed_http_status.claim: A BadStatusLine before valid response headers is an unreachable provider attempt with null status and no EXECUTED state.
malformed_http_status.counterhypothesis: Only timeout, URL and connection exceptions can occur before a response; falsified because BadStatusLine is an independent HTTPException and escaped without a receipt.

transport_os_errors.claim: Transport-layer OSError failures such as ssl.SSLError before response headers are unreachable provider attempts with null status and no EXECUTED state.
transport_os_errors.counterhypothesis: urllib always wraps TLS failures in URLError or ConnectionError; falsified by the executable opener path where SSLError propagated directly without a receipt.

transport_post_replay_safety.claim: A Chat Completions POST with a transport or response-read failure is not automatically retryable unless the client can prove the original request was never applied or the operation is idempotent.
transport_post_replay_safety.counterhypothesis: No response bytes or an incomplete response proves the POST was not applied and makes blind retry safe; falsified because RemoteDisconnected describes failure while reading the response, and the adapter cannot observe whether the provider already processed the request.

generic_provider_error_replay_safety.claim: Generic 4xx and 5xx responses to a non-idempotent Chat Completions POST are not automatically retryable; a received status never proves replay safety.
generic_provider_error_replay_safety.counterhypothesis: Every non-429 provider error becomes safe to replay after a short cooldown; falsified because unchanged 4xx requests require request, credential or policy correction, while a 5xx response does not prove that the original POST had no application-side effects.

rate_limit_retry_after.claim: A received HTTP 429 Retry-After field controls when a later request may be attempted and is parsed in either delay-seconds or HTTP-date form across regular-response and HTTPError paths. Absolute HTTP-date cooldown is calculated from response receipt time, not request start; neither form authorizes automatic replay of the same non-idempotent POST.
rate_limit_retry_after.counterhypothesis: Retry-After both supplies the cooldown and proves that identical POST replay is safe, or an HTTP-date can be subtracted from request start; falsified because RFC 6585 only describes when to make a new request, RFC 9110 separately requires replay-safety evidence, and a 100-second request inflated a 40-second remaining window to 140 seconds.

oversized_retry_after.claim: Retry-After metadata is limited to 128 characters before normalization, digit scanning or HTTP-date parsing. Larger values use the conservative 60-second fallback and cannot impose unbounded post-response parsing work or suppress the received HTTP 429 receipt.
oversized_retry_after.counterhypothesis: An exact built-in string is bounded enough to pass to Retry-After parsers after a received response; falsified locally because a 129-character syntactically impossible value reached parsedate_to_datetime after HTTP 429. A 100-digit delay remains accepted and safely caps to 86400 seconds.

retry_after_header_access_failure.claim: Failure while reading Retry-After metadata from a transport adapter cannot suppress or reclassify an already received HTTP 429; regular-response and HTTPError paths retain rate_limited plus EXECUTED and use the conservative 60-second fallback.
retry_after_header_access_failure.counterhypothesis: Header lookup is total once an adapter exposes a headers object; falsified by an injected mapping-compatible adapter whose get operation raises ValueError: the regular-response path changed 429 to invalid_provider_response and the HTTPError path escaped without a receipt.

passive_retry_after_value_boundary.claim: A Retry-After value returned by a transport adapter must be an exact built-in string before parsing; polymorphic string subclasses use the conservative 60-second fallback without executing overridden methods, reclassifying the received HTTP 429 or suppressing its receipt.
passive_retry_after_value_boundary.counterhypothesis: isinstance(value, str) proves that a transport-provided Retry-After value is passive text; falsified locally because a str subclass executed its overridden strip method, downgraded a regular 429 to incomplete_provider_response and escaped the HTTPError path without a receipt.

response_header_property_failure.claim: The transport adapter's headers attribute is optional metadata behind a potentially executable descriptor. Failure while retrieving that property cannot suppress or reclassify an already received HTTP 429; both response forms use the 60-second fallback and retain EXECUTED.
response_header_property_failure.counterhypothesis: Catching failures from the header mapping's get method fully contains untrusted metadata access; falsified because a property descriptor can raise before a mapping object is returned, causing regular 429 misclassification and an escaped HTTPError path.

response_status_property_failure.claim: Status and code attributes supplied by a transport adapter are executable metadata lookups. If retrieval fails, the adapter emits invalid_provider_response with null status and without EXECUTED, rather than escaping without a receipt or inventing a status.
response_status_property_failure.counterhypothesis: Status and HTTPError code attributes are passive values and cannot fail during access; falsified by response and HTTPError property descriptors whose RuntimeError escaped both receipt paths.

passive_http_status_value_boundary.claim: HTTP status metadata must be an exact built-in integer before range or classification comparisons; boolean and polymorphic integer values fail closed with null status and without EXECUTED, and no overridden comparison operator may run.
passive_http_status_value_boundary.counterhypothesis: isinstance(value, int) plus excluding bool proves that transport status is passive numeric metadata; falsified locally because an int subclass executed its overridden comparison operator, changed the regular response to unreachable_provider and escaped the HTTPError path without a receipt.

unexpected_transport_adapter_failure.claim: A custom transport adapter can raise an Exception outside urllib's documented hierarchy. The outer execution boundary emits unreachable_provider before a valid response or incomplete_provider_response after valid status metadata, remains nonretryable, and deliberately does not catch BaseException process-control signals.
unexpected_transport_adapter_failure.counterhypothesis: URLError, OSError and HTTPException cover every opener, context-manager and body-read failure; falsified by custom adapter RuntimeError before response and during body read, both of which escaped without receipts.

bounded_retry_after_cooldown.claim: Retry-After cooldown metadata is bounded to 86400 seconds in receipts for both delay-seconds and HTTP-date forms; the nonretryable request requires fresh operator or scheduler evaluation beyond that horizon.
bounded_retry_after_cooldown.counterhypothesis: Syntactically valid Retry-After values are inherently operationally bounded; falsified by a 100-digit delay and a year-9999 HTTP-date that produced unbounded receipt integers on both response paths.

http_status_validation.claim: A provider adapter must supply an integer HTTP status from 100 through 599 before the body is consumed or EXECUTED is asserted; missing, boolean, textual and out-of-range values are invalid.
http_status_validation.counterhypothesis: A missing adapter status can safely default to 200 and Python isinstance(value, int) is sufficient; falsified because missing status verified arbitrary content and bool is an int subclass.

http_response_body_type.claim: The HTTP adapter body must be bytes before JSON parsing; text and bytearray values are invalid transport responses even when they contain valid JSON.
http_response_body_type.counterhypothesis: Successful json.loads parsing proves a valid HTTP body; falsified because json.loads intentionally accepts str and bytearray in addition to bytes.

passive_http_response_body_boundary.claim: A transport-provided HTTP response body must be an exact built-in bytes value before size measurement or UTF-8 decoding; bytes subclasses remain invalid_provider_response and no overridden length or decode method may execute.
passive_http_response_body_boundary.counterhypothesis: isinstance(value, bytes) proves that an adapter body is passive immutable transport data; falsified locally because a bytes subclass executed its overridden __len__ after HTTP 200 and changed invalid adapter metadata into incomplete_provider_response.

network_json_encoding.claim: Network-transmitted provider JSON is decoded strictly as UTF-8 before parsing; UTF-16 and UTF-32 response bodies cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
network_json_encoding.counterhypothesis: Passing response bytes directly to Python json.loads enforces the network JSON encoding contract; falsified because the decoder automatically recognized UTF-16 and UTF-32 bodies and both reached success, VERIFIED and DONE.

strict_json_numbers.claim: Provider response JSON containing NaN, Infinity, -Infinity or an exponent that overflows the runtime float range is invalid and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
strict_json_numbers.counterhypothesis: Rejecting the nonstandard NaN and Infinity literals through parse_constant is sufficient to keep non-finite values out; falsified because CPython decodes RFC-grammar exponents such as 1e400 through the separate default float path and produced infinity that reached success, VERIFIED and DONE.

unique_json_object_names.claim: Provider response objects with duplicate member names are ambiguous across parsers and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
unique_json_object_names.counterhypothesis: Python's last-name-wins behavior is a safe canonical interpretation; falsified as a portability claim because RFC 8259 documents error, last-only and all-pairs behaviors as interoperably unpredictable.

json_nesting_failure_receipts.claim: Excessively nested provider JSON that reaches Python's recursion limit must emit invalid_provider_response rather than escape without an execution receipt.
json_nesting_failure_receipts.counterhypothesis: The 2000000-byte response limit is sufficient to bound every JSON parser failure; falsified by a roughly 40000-byte, 20000-level array that raised RecursionError without a receipt.

unicode_scalar_text_boundaries.claim: Text-chat request and response strings must contain Unicode scalar values; lone UTF-16 surrogates cannot cross the authenticated request boundary or reach VERIFIED/DONE.
unicode_scalar_text_boundaries.counterhypothesis: Successful Python json.loads parsing proves an interoperable Unicode string; falsified because an escaped lone surrogate was decoded as str and reached success/VERIFIED/DONE even though RFC 8259 calls receiver behavior unpredictable.

plain_text_message_fields.claim: The plain-text adapter accepts exactly role and content in each message; tool_calls, tool_call_id, name, reasoning_content and future extension fields require an explicitly typed adapter.
plain_text_message_fields.counterhypothesis: Validating role and content is enough for a text-only adapter; falsified because an assistant message carrying tool_calls passed unchanged to the authenticated network opener.

nonempty_text_conversation.claim: NVIDIA Chat Completions requires messages to contain at least one item; an empty conversation is rejected before credential use or network access.
nonempty_text_conversation.counterhypothesis: Provider-side validation is sufficient; falsified because an empty messages list reached the authenticated opener and caused an avoidable network attempt.

nonblank_text_message_content.claim: Every role/content message handled by this plain-text adapter requires nonblank scalar text before credential use or network access. This is a fail-closed adapter rule, not an additional NVIDIA schema claim: empty content can have meaning only in typed tool or multimodal paths, which this adapter rejects separately.
nonblank_text_message_content.counterhypothesis: Provider-side validation or an empty text message is sufficient for this adapter; falsified locally because empty and whitespace-only user content both reached the authenticated opener despite carrying no typed tool or multimodal payload.

text_conversation_sequence.claim: NVIDIA Chat Completions requires user and assistant messages to alternate, the final input message to have role user, and an optional system message to be first; invalid sequences are rejected before credential use or network access.
text_conversation_sequence.counterhypothesis: Validating each role independently is sufficient; falsified because assistant-ended, consecutive-user and late-system conversations all reached the authenticated opener despite violating the documented conversation grammar.

plain_text_response_fields.claim: A text-only response message requires role assistant plus scalar content only; missing authorship, tool_calls and other typed response extensions cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE through this adapter.
plain_text_response_fields.counterhypothesis: A nonempty content string plus terminal finish reason is sufficient proof of a complete text response; falsified because both a response carrying tool_calls and a response without assistant authorship reached success/VERIFIED/DONE.

closed_text_response_choice_schema.claim: FRANK v0.1's non-streaming plain-text adapter requires finish_reason and message, permits NVIDIA's documented index=0 plus null logprobs, stop_reason and token_ids metadata, and rejects any unknown or semantically unhandled choice field before VERIFIED or DONE.
